name: Zstandard
summary: An exact-upstream Zstandard 1.5.7 compression/decompression WebAssembly canary; browser-core validation is in progress.

zoo.provenance: in-toto Statement + SLSA Provenance v1 (pending CI validation)

profiles.label: Browser Core (canary)
features: exact upstream libzstd 1.5.7 compression and decompression
profiles.output: Experimental Zstandard compression/decompression library, not yet a generic CLI or published package

comparison.name: Upstream native
comparison.note: Reference libzstd C library and full CLI, native filesystem and optional multithreading.

comparison.name: WASM Zoo
comparison.note: Experimental libzstd C API browser-core target only; public release pending CI review.

notes: Canary does not claim a published release, npm artifact, or cross-browser validation until the actual upstream build and browser smoke gates pass.
The popular third-party zstd-codec source pins upstream Zstandard 1.3.6; its npm tarball's exact embedded core should be inspected separately before making a binary-level comparison.
Full upstream zstd CLI, streaming and dictionary workflows are separate rollout gates; this first target exposes safe one-shot compression/decompression only.
No cross-origin isolation is required by this single-threaded profile; never automatically publish based on successful candidate CI.

referenceWasm.name: zstd-codec
referenceWasm.note: The third-party source repository's cpp/zstd submodule points to commit 4fa456d7f12f8b27bd3b2f5dfd4f46898cb31c24 (v1.3.6). This is source-pin evidence, not a binary audit of npm.

capabilityMatrix.note: Canary uses upstream libzstd's one-shot C API; real browser roundtrip and frame-magic assertions are CI gates.
The initial one-shot API requires a known content size for decompression. Streaming will be a separate reviewed phase.
Upstream has dictionary APIs but this first browser-core wrapper intentionally does not expose them.

capabilityMatrix.feature: Upstream zstd CLI and native filesystem
capabilityMatrix.note: Initial canary is a C-library wrapper rather than a CLI. Host files are never exposed.
Initial browser-core is single-threaded in an outer Worker, so COOP/COEP is not required.
No runtime network API; local core and WASM resources are fetched by the browser.
